title: Inflammatory Pathways Modulated by Prenatal Mindfulness: A Route to Improve Maternal Child Emotional Well Being and Whole Person Health
official: Inflammatory Pathways Modulated by Prenatal Mindfulness: A Route to Improve Maternal Child Emotional Well Being and Whole Person Health
summary: The goal of this study is to investigate inflammation as the biological mechanism by which mindfulness based cognitive therapy for perinatal depression (MBCT-PD) administered during pregnancy improves women's emotional well-being and whole person health index during pregnancy and the early postpartum period. Secondarily the investigative team will determine if MBCT-PD administered during pregnancy improves the physical health and emotional well-being of the developing child.

interventions.name: Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for perinatal depression

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Pregnant women aged 18-50 in good health.
* Individuals who do not expect to move over the next year.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Pregnancies deemed high risk due to multiple pregnancies, medical conditions such as type 1 or 2 diabetes, mellitus, cancer, hypertension, kidney disease, and epilepsy, the presence of infections (HIV, hepatitis C), history of three or more miscarriages, or if the fetus has been diagnosed with a genetic condition such as Down syndrome.
* Smoking (\>5 cigarettes during pregnancy),
* Drinking alcohol (\>10 drinks during pregnancy)
* Marijuana use (legal in Oregon),
* Reported illicit drug use
